options.name: Desert Night Soul
options.sound: Slow-burning cinematic desert blues: tremolo baritone guitar, frame drum and hand claps, upright bass, a smoky low female vocal; the last chorus opens into a wide, gospel-tinged group answer.
options.feeling: Heat leaving the sand after dark. Patient, a little dangerous, then warm.
options.suno: cinematic desert blues, tremolo baritone guitar, frame drum, handclaps, upright bass, smoky low female vocal, gospel group chorus, slow burn, 72 bpm

options.name: Harbor Lights City Pop
options.sound: Bright 1980s-style city pop: slap bass, Rhodes piano, glassy chorus guitar, short brass stabs, a light male–female duet trading lines and meeting on the hook.
options.feeling: A late ferry ride into a lit-up harbor, windows down, nothing urgent.
options.tempo: about 112 BPM, steady four-on-the-floor lift in the chorus
options.suno: 80s city pop, slap bass, rhodes piano, glassy chorus guitar, brass stabs, male female duet, bright, breezy, 112 bpm

options.name: Cathedral Breaks
options.sound: Starts as a still choir over an organ drone and bells, then drops into fast, liquid drum and bass: rolling breakbeats, deep sub, chopped choir phrases over the top.
options.feeling: Stone and stained glass suddenly running. Awe that turns into motion.
options.suno: choral ambient intro, organ drone, bells, then liquid drum and bass, rolling breakbeats, deep sub bass, chopped choir vocals, euphoric, 172 bpm

decision.words: None of them. Something more like the musical style in Monolith, The Resonance Chamber or When the Wires Wake, with the artistic style of Monolith.

direction.name: Dark Industrial Electronica, Monumental Ink
direction.sound: Dark industrial electronica and cinematic darksynth in the family of Monolith (Horizon), The Resonance Chamber (Horizon) and When the Wires Wake (Astra): a heavy half-time stride, saturated detuned analog sub-bass, dry crushing kick, cavernous snare, ticking metallic percussion, cold granular pads, and a low, intimate voice inside the machinery. Original melody and lyric; none of those recordings are used.
direction.art: Monolith's look: monochrome architectural pen-and-ink, brutalist megastructures, cables and conduits as the performers, a small human figure for scale; charcoal, slate and bone paper with one restrained accent colour. New plates only; none of Monolith's art is used.
direction.tempo: about 138 BPM, felt as a 69 BPM half-time stride
direction.suno: dark industrial electronica, cinematic darksynth, 138 bpm half-time stride, saturated detuned analog sub-bass, dry crushing kick, cavernous snare, ticking metallic percussion, cold granular pads, low intimate baritone vocal, minor key, vast negative space, nocturnal
